successCriteria.description: The `create` method in `balance.service.ts` rejects a `CreateBalanceDto` whose `totalEntitlement` is not an integer by throwing a `ValidationError` with a descriptive message.

The existing test "should floor fractional totalEntitlement" in `tests/unit/modules/balance/balance.service.test.ts` is replaced with a test that expects a `ValidationError` when `totalEntitlement` is fractional (e.g., 15.7).

constraints: The `ValidationError` class already defined in `balance.service.ts` must be reused — do not introduce a new error type.
The `totalEntitlement` validation guard in `create` must use `!Number.isInteger(data.totalEntitlement)` — consistent with the existing `fiscalYear` integer check pattern already in the same method.
No other method signatures, return types, or exported symbols in the balance module may change. This is a validation-only change confined to the `create` method body and its corresponding test.
outOfScope: Changing validation in `deductDays`, `restoreDays`, or `hasSufficientBalance` — those methods continue to floor fractional `days`/`requestedDays` inputs as they do today.

entityInvariants.invariant: `totalEntitlement` must be a positive integer at creation time. Fractional values are rejected at the service boundary with a `ValidationError` rather than silently floored.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws `ValidationError` for: empty/whitespace-only employeeId, empty/whitespace-only leavePolicyId, non-positive or non-finite totalEntitlement, non-integer totalEntitlement, non-positive or non-integer fiscalYear.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The new `!Number.isInteger(data.totalEntitlement)` check must follow the same guard pattern as the existing `!Number.isInteger(data.fiscalYear)` check on line 42 of `balance.service.ts` — same predicate, same error-throwing style, same placement within the validation block.
